## Data

A synthetic 12 by 8 km area on a local grid in meters, with no real location and no CRS. {{< var x001.ncap >}} land-capability parcels (classes 1–7) and {{< var x001.nuse >}} land-use parcels (forest, cropland, pasture, wetland, settlement), made from seeded Voronoi partitions.

## Results

| Representation | Method | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Two map images, 60 m cells | Pixel coincidence count, with the sheet width supplied from outside the image | {{< var x001.img200 >}} ha ({{< var x001.err200 >}}% off) |
| Two map images, 12 m cells | Same | {{< var x001.img1000 >}} ha ({{< var x001.err1000 >}}% off) |
| Coordinate and attribute tables | Shoelace areas per parcel | Class 1–2 total {{< var x001.class12 >}} ha; forest total {{< var x001.forest >}} ha; overlap not computable without polygon intersection |
| GeoPackage + DuckDB Spatial | One SQL query | {{< var x001.exact >}} ha |
| GeoPackage + GeoPandas overlay | Independent check | {{< var x001.check >}} ha |

## Files

- [`run.py`](run.py) builds the data, runs all three methods and writes [`results.json`](results.json).
- [`figures.py`](figures.py) draws the article's answer figure.
- [`data/x001.gpkg`](data/x001.gpkg) holds both layers. The same parcels as plain tables: [`capability_vertices.csv`](data/capability_vertices.csv), [`capability_attributes.csv`](data/capability_attributes.csv), [`land_use_vertices.csv`](data/land_use_vertices.csv) and [`land_use_attributes.csv`](data/land_use_attributes.csv).
- [`requirements.txt`](requirements.txt) pins the environment.

## Limitations

The image method is idealized: the sheets are drawn without antialiasing and read back by exact color, which is kinder than any scan of a printed map. The test says nothing about performance; nothing was timed.
